clue.text: Roman general had a hold on father

parts.note: a grip is a hold, so 'a hold' gives the article plus the grasp
pa is an informal word for one's father

explanation.surface: A Roman commander kept a firm grip on his dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' and 'on' are link words: A GRIP placed before PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was a celebrated Roman general and admiral under Augustus.

clue.text: British-born poet takes gold to hideout

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a den is a secret lair or hideout

explanation.surface: A poet carries his treasure off to a secret lair.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was a poet born in York who later took American citizenship.

clue.text: Standard artillery pistol held up

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
a Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol

explanation.surface: A gunman holds up a bank with an ordinary army pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns the whole run RALUGER backwards, giving REGUL then AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular and standard are synonyms for the usual or normal kind.

clue.text: Urns appearing in final note about Old Testament

indicators.note: about means going round, so the note's letters are wrapped around the testament's

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Urns are mentioned in a closing note about the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: A postscript is the note that comes last in a letter; 'appearing in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots and urns are both vessels for holding things, urns being a kind of pot.

clue.text: Healthy because of certain people — a statement of envy

parts.note: all right can mean in good health
for can mean because of, as in 'jumped for joy'
some means certain unspecified people

explanation.surface: Some people get to be healthy, an envious onlooker grumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a rueful remark made by someone jealous of another's good luck.

clue.text: Press a loose woman for something sweet

parts.note: to jam is to press or squeeze tightly
tart is a slang term for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: Squeezing up against a woman of easy virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam tart is a pastry filled with jam, a sweet treat.

clue.text: Right Honourable cronies: they do not love each other

definitions.text: they do not love each other

parts.note: just means right or fair
good can mean honourable or virtuous
cronies are close friends

explanation.surface: Members of parliament addressed as Right Honourable are chummy but feel no affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right Honourable' looks like the title of a British MP or minister, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock denial couples give when asked about a romance.

clue.text: Destroy moth in sack, which is waterproof

indicators.note: destroying the words breaks them up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kill the moth trapped in the bag, which keeps out rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroy' rearranges MOTH IN SACK; 'which is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a raincoat, and 'waterproof' as a noun also means a raincoat.

clue.text: A man needs it: a mushroom

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fellow requires it, a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces A, MAN, IT and A are all given as written; 'needs' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanita is a genus of mushrooms including the fly agaric and death cap.

clue.text: Ted, about to eat up, made a noise

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so Ted goes round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: to gnaw is to eat by biting

explanation.surface: Ted, about to gobble something, made a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ted, about to eat' reads as Ted on the verge of eating, but 'about' is the container signal and 'up' the reversal; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Twanged describes the ringing sound of a plucked string, so it means made a noise.

clue.text: To understand nearly all of Italy is a drug

parts.note: dig is slang for understand

indicators.note: nearly all means the word is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: Grasping most of Italy involves a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis is a heart drug extracted from foxglove.

clue.text: Left in a vehicle with a bright girl

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A clever girl was left in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'a' is a link; the second 'a' supplies the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The name Clara derives from the Latin for bright or clear.

clue.text: Duck starting to eat in river

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, i.e. nil

indicators.note: starting to means only the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A duck begins to eat in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a duck is a batsman's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa.

clue.text: Dig us out and I squeal, being in hiding

indicators.note: out signals that the preceding letters are disordered

parts.note: to squeal or sing is slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: Dig us out and I'll inform, says a cornered crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DIGUS into DISGU; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Disguising oneself is masking one's identity, a form of being in hiding.

clue.text: Coffee break to fill pause, getting too favourable an impression

indicators.note: to fill means to go inside, so these letters sit within the pause

parts.note: a halt is a pause or stop

indicators.note: break means the letters are broken up and reshaped

explanation.surface: A coffee break fills a pause in work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coffee break' looks like one phrase, but 'break' is the anagram signal; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The halo effect is a bias where one good trait colours the whole judgement of someone.

clue.text: Making water hot for band

indicators.note: making the letters into something new means rearranging them

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Getting water hot for the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath is a ring or band, as of flowers.

clue.text: Known drawback is superficial

parts.note: out means known or revealed, as in 'the secret is out'

indicators.note: back signals the word before it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A known drawback is merely surface-deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' looks like one word but splits into DRAW and its reversal signal 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Outward means on the surface or external, so is a synonym of superficial.

clue.text: Dismissed fifty with help not available

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
aid is help
off means not available, as of a dish on a menu

explanation.surface: Fifty workers were dismissed with no help available.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid off means made redundant, i.e. dismissed from a job.

clue.text: Short account retained by Colin craftily

indicators.note: retained by means held inside the other piece
craftily means slyly, so the name's letters are cunningly rearranged

explanation.surface: Colin cunningly kept a brief account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftily' rearranges the name into LONIC before the account goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic means using few words, so it is short or terse in speech.

clue.text: Hostility is damaging to pleasure

parts.note: ill means harmful, as in 'ill effects'
will means wish or pleasure, as in 'at his will'

explanation.surface: Hostility spoils enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will means enmity or animosity, so it is hostility.

clue.text: One who does not eat quicker

definitions.meaning: a person going without food deliberately

explanation.definitionFit: Someone abstaining from food is a faster, and the comparative of fast is quicker.

clue.text: Survey's clean but nonsense

parts.note: to eye is to survey or look over; 's is a link
to wash is to clean

explanation.surface: An inspection says it's clean, but it's rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is slang for nonsense or humbug.

clue.text: Part of leg keeps one on air, dancing, in a state

indicators.note: a leg that keeps something holds it within, so the numeral sits inside the leg part

parts.note: the calf is the back of the lower leg
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leg kept aloft while dancing in some region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges ON AIR into ORNIA; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: California is a state on the west coast of the USA.

clue.text: Witnesses coming into view from left and right

indicators.text: coming into view from left and right
indicators.note: the word looks the same whether it is read from the left or from the right

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Witnesses appear from both sides of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Sees is a verb meaning witnesses or observes.

clue.text: It's thick, so put on top

parts.note: taken as written
a lid is a top or cover

explanation.surface: It's dense, so put a cover on.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid means dense or thick, not liquid or thin.

clue.text: A party — Galatea is wanting a cuppa

indicators.note: is wanting means lacking, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Galatea fancies a cup of tea at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: Galatea is a sea nymph of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive party or celebration.

clue.text: Racket used by champion needing short set

parts.note: a champion is the number one, written No. 1 or NOI

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end

explanation.surface: A tennis racket used by the champion in a brief set.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din or noise.

clue.text: Horribly vain and aloof, but not successful

indicators.note: horribly shows the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone appallingly vain and standoffish, but a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Of no avail means fruitless or ineffective, so unsuccessful.

clue.text: French writer having care of unfinished letter

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the abbreviation for care of on letters

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is lost

explanation.surface: A French author is minding an incomplete letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Colette was a French novelist, author of Gigi.

clue.text: This is drunk with second type of potatoes

parts.note: mashed potatoes are a common way of serving potatoes

explanation.surface: This is consumed with a second helping of potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as a verb but is the definition, an adjective; 'This is' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed is slang for very drunk.
